description: City of Cape Town live cadastral source contract, identity and bounded query verification.
sourceScope: City of Cape Town municipal cadastral parcels; duplicate address rows with the same SG26 code and identical geometry collapse to one parcel. Conflicting geometry fails closed. Other South African municipalities use separate sources.

catalogueItem.title: Land Parcels
catalogueItem.descriptionSummary: City cadastre information populated by various departments; detailed parcel geometries, unique identifiers and legal/administrative attributes. Hub item says spatial layers are served live from internal systems; the item's Last Updated/Publish Date describes metadata only.
catalogueItem.reuseAndAttributionAssessment: The dataset metadata points to the City's open-data terms, but that exact URL currently returns HTTP 404. The City Open Data Policy says portal Terms of Use will conform with open-data principles and access is free without prior registration; however the linked operative dataset terms could not be read. The general City website Terms of Use page is broader website content language (all-rights-reserved; limits redistribution/commercial exploitation) and does not clearly resolve reuse rights for this specific open-data layer. Do not assign an OS/CC/open-government license or claim commercial reuse permission until the dataset-specific terms are recovered/confirmed. Cautious attribution if later permitted: City of Cape Town, Land Parcels, via City of Cape Town Open Data Portal.
termsEvidence: The dataset-specific Terms of Use URL returns 404 with/without trailing slash and case variant at check date.

Official Open Data Policy search-indexed clause 7.6 says portal use is subject to Terms of Use which conform with open-data principles; clause 7.7 says access is free and does not require prior registration. It does not supply a clear dataset reuse license or attribution text.

The current general Terms of Use page says website/content copyright is City property, permits personal non-commercial extracts/copies with acknowledgment, and says distribution/commercial exploitation requires express written permission. It is a general web-content notice; applicability to this separately licensed Open Data Portal dataset is unresolved.
catalogueItem.accessInformation: Development Management, Business Enablement, City of Cape Town (as shown in ArcGIS sharing item)

layerMetadata.nativeStableKeyCandidate: SG26_CODE (26-char Surveyor-General cadastral code); do not confuse with volatile OBJECTID. Old research's 21-char note is stale.
layerMetadata.sampleKeyPattern: ^[A-Z0-9]{26}$ (sampled values uppercase alphanumeric, including terminal RE suffix; whole-layer exhaustive pattern validation not performed)
layerMetadata.sourceScope: City of Cape Town metropolitan municipality, not all South Africa. Hub item polygon extent bounds the metro area.
layerMetadata.parcelType: City cadastre / cadastral erf or land parcel polygons with legal-status and address/zoning attributes; not ownership/owner names.
layerMetadata.updateCadence: No reliable cadence. Hub item's narrative says live from internal systems; metadata dates refer to metadata only.

identity.uniquenessAssessment: SG26_CODE, SL_LAND_PRCL_KEY and PRTY_NMBR all have repeated values globally; they are not unique feature-row keys. In four sampled repeated SG26_CODE groups, all returned rows had identical geometry; rows carried repeated cadastral IDs but varying address values. The current adapter by-ID geometry dedup would collapse these to one canonical parcel feature; this makes SG26_CODE viable as a parcel identity for those repeated groups. This does not prove every repeated-key group has identical geometry; any repeat with differing geometry would trigger the adapter's conflicting-geometry error and requires a check on the larger source area.
identity.countDistinctStatisticAttempt: ArcGIS returned invalid outStatistics for countdistinct despite advertising supportsCountDistinct=true; no whole-layer distinct-key total established.
identity.duplicateAggregates: Whole-layer grouped aggregate confirms many duplicate key groups (response exceeded result transfer limit); OBJECTID is the only field with unique index.

license.note: Official public open-data item; named reuse licence not established. Linked City open-data terms page returned 404 at verification.
